data.title: Security Advisory: Uncontrolled Recursion Depth in Tree Walkers Leads to Stack-Overflow DoS
data.body:
## Summary

`braces` 3.0.3 bounds only input character length (`MAX_LENGTH = 10000`), not brace nesting depth. Its recursive AST walkers use one stack frame per nesting level with no depth guard. A short, deeply-nested pattern under the character cap exhausts the call stack and throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`; uncaught, this terminates the Node process. Verified on Node v26.5.0 / `braces@3.0.3`: `compile` (the default `braces()` path) crashes at depth ≥ ~3500 and `expand` at ≥ ~4000, both within the 10,000-char cap.

- **Component:** braces
- **Affected version:** <= 3.0.3
- **CWE:** CWE-674 (Uncontrolled Recursion); CWE-400 (Uncontrolled Resource Consumption)
- **Attack vector:** Untrusted deeply-nested brace pattern from an unauthenticated caller


## Description

`parse()` caps characters (`lib/parse.js:37-39`) but never nesting depth. Each nested `{` produces a `brace` node containing another `brace` node, and each output path walks the tree recursively:

```js
// lib/compile.js:48-52 — default braces() path, no depth guard
if (node.nodes) {
  for (const child of node.nodes) {
    output += walk(child, node);   // one frame per nesting level
  }
}
```

The recursion is synchronous and driven purely by input depth. A few thousand nesting levels, far below the character cap, exceed the engine's stack limit. `expand.js:102-104` shares the same recursion and crashes at depth ≥ ~4000. `stringify.js:22-26` is structurally identical but does not overflow within the character cap (its lighter frames survive to the maximum depth of ~5000 the cap allows), so the exploitable sinks are `compile` and `expand`.

The README documents `options.maxLength` (default 10,000) only as a *character* guard, and its "Brace matching pitfalls" section covers only expansion *output size*. No depth bound is documented and there is no `maxDepth` option. These inputs stay under the character cap yet crash in default `braces()` compile mode, because the fault is in AST walk recursion. The library already validates malformed input via `MAX_LENGTH`; depth is the same class of guard, left incomplete.


## Recommended Fix

- Enforce a maximum brace nesting depth in `parse()` (e.g. throw above ~100), analogous to the existing character cap. This bounds every downstream walker at the source.
- Optionally convert the walk/stringify recursion to an explicit iterative stack.
- Until a fixed release: set `options.maxLength` far below 10,000 and/or reject patterns whose `{` nesting exceeds a small bound before calling `braces()`.

## Reference

- CWE-674 (Uncontrolled Recursion); CWE-400 (Uncontrolled Resource Consumption)
- Related (distinct: token count vs. nesting depth): CVE-2024-4068 / GHSA-grv7-fg5c-xmjg

## Overview
[braces](https://www.npmjs.com/package/braces) is a Bash-like brace expansion, implemented in JavaScript.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Uncontrolled Recursion in the recursive AST walkers, which lack depth guards. An attacker can supply deeply nested brace patterns that stay within the character limit to exhaust the call stack and crash the Node.js process with an uncaught `RangeError`.
## Remediation
There is no fixed version for `braces`.
## References
- [GitHub Issue](https://github.com/micromatch/braces/issues/70)
- [Vulnerable Code](https://github.com/micromatch/braces/blob/3.0.3/lib/compile.js#L49-L53)
- [Vulnerable Code](https://github.com/micromatch/braces/blob/3.0.3/lib/expand.js#L102-L105)
- [Vulnerable Code](https://github.com/micromatch/braces/blob/3.0.3/lib/parse.js#L38-L40)

issue.body:
## Summary

Fixes CVE-2026-93687 and closes #70.

`braces` through 3.0.3 allows an attacker-controlled, deeply nested brace pattern to exhaust the JavaScript call stack in its recursive AST walkers. Because the payload fits under the existing 10,000-character input limit, an unauthenticated attacker can trigger an uncaught `RangeError` and terminate the Node.js process, causing a denial of service.

## Fix

- Limit brace and parenthesis nesting to 100 levels while parsing.
- Apply the same limit to `compile`, `expand`, and `stringify` so caller-supplied ASTs cannot bypass parser validation.
- Allow callers to configure a stricter `maxDepth` while capping larger values at the safe maximum.
- Document the new `maxDepth` option.
- Add regression coverage for string inputs, direct AST inputs, and the allowed boundary.

## Verification

The complete Mocha test suite passes: **899 passing tests**, including the new parser, compile, expand, and stringify depth-limit regression tests. Targeted public-API boundary checks, JavaScript syntax checks, and whitespace checks also pass.
